canonical_question: What specific strain rates were compared in the investigation of the 'anomalous behavior' at 300 K?

question_variants.question: What specific strain rates were compared in the investigation of the 'anomalous behavior' at 300 K?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The investigation at 300 K compared three specific strain rates: 10^8, 10^9, and 10^10 s^-1. The text notes that these rates were used to investigate anomalous behavior via CNA and DXA analyses.

answers.answer: The specific strain rates compared in the investigation of anomalous behavior at 300 K were 10^8 s^-1, 10^9 s^-1, and 10^10 s^-1. CNA and DXA analyses were performed on the alloy model at 300 K under these different strain rates.
answers.processing_state: Single crystal bulk model, Equilibrium FCC structure
answers.measurement_outcome: Analyses performed to investigate anomalous behavior at different strain rates (10^8, 10^9, 10^10 s^-1)
answers.mechanism: CNA and DXA analyses used to characterize structural changes under different strain rates
answers.boundary_limitation: Simulations conducted at nanoscale with high strain rates; may not capture macroscopic sensitivity.
evidence_spans: The primary dislocations observed were Shockley partial dislocations and stair-rod immobile dislocations.
No BCC atoms were observed in any of the three orientations, indicating that no FCC-to-BCC phase transformation occurred during tensile deformation.
The yield strength of the alloy was relatively insensitive to strain rate within the simulated range.
